notes: Identity checked: full primary research-article text, pp. 859–869, Kyla Haimovitz and Carol S. Dweck, Psychological Science 2016, 27(6), DOI 10.1177/0956797616639727. The printed title is “What Predicts Children’s Fixed and Growth Intelligence Mind-Sets? Not Their Parents’ Views of Intelligence but Their Parents’ Views of Failure”, differing from the supplied reference title; authors, DOI, year, journal, volume and pagination match. No PDF supplied; no rendering performed. The description concerns children’s intelligence mind-sets and parents’ views of failure, whereas Study 4 tests parents’ responses; the p. 7 locator also includes Study 3b results. This conflict does not identify one critical test. Study 4 has multiple distinct tests: manipulation check t(124) = 2.53, p = 0.013; performance-oriented response t(131) = 3.246, p < .001, printed partial eta-squared .075; learning-oriented response t(131) = −2.04, p = .043, printed partial eta-squared .031; competence-controlled responses t(131) = 3.249, p = .002 and t(1, 131) = −2.02, p = .046. Preserve these as printed, including unusual degrees of freedom. No test is assigned by row order. The Study 4 method gives 132 recruited parents selected from 310 adults; it does not explicitly establish final analytic N for an identified target test, and N is not inferred from df. Study 3b on PDF p. 7 / printed p. 865 instead concerns children’s perceptions of parents’ failure mind-sets and children’s own intelligence mind-sets (beta 0.30, p = .003; competence-controlled beta 0.26, p = .010), with a sample of 100 children. These are alternate-study candidates only. Only n_o and pval_value_o are assigned; other fields are placeholders.
